append.text: **Ps 34:1 *Júdica, Dómine, nocéntes me* → *Julgai, Senhor, os que me fazem mal*** — the object asked for the clause, as the row foresaw (Matos Soares 1932 word for word; DRB 'them that wrong me'). The Introit / Tract of Passion Monday. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 34:10b — all three in one verse: *Erípiens ínopem … egénum et páuperem* → *Vós que arrancais o carente … o necessitado e o pobre*.** Draft 1 tried *desvalido* (Matos Soares 1932): unknown to the blind reader, like *indigente* before it. Draft 2 *carente* passed the Latinist. **Proposal for the row: inops → *carente* (known, and apart from *pobre* and *necessitado*); *indigente* has now failed three blind readers and *desvalido* one.**

**Ps 34:16 *tentavérunt me* (men trying the psalmist) → *puseram-me à prova*** (Matos Soares 1932): draft 1's *tentaram-me* was heard first by the blind reader as 'tried to lead me into sin' — the 25:2 fault again. Passed the Latinist. So the row has three: *experimentar* (God tests), *tentar* (men tempt God), *pôr à prova* (men try a man).

**Ps 34:17 *restítue ánimam meam* → *Trazei de volta a minha alma*:** *restituí* is also 'I restored' (rule 3), so the imperative cannot take the row's verb; draft 1 *Restaurai* was unclear to the stylist (*restaurar da maldade*). Passed the Latinist. *Restaurai* and *Fazei voltar* are options. The Tuesday Matins antiphon *Restítue ánimam meam * a malefáctis eórum, Dómine* is another Latin (grep) and will want the same verb.
Ps 34:17 copied: *a minha única, dos leões* (the object first, as 21:21; no *e*, which the Latin lacks here). Heard 'my one soul'.
Ps 34:3 *conclúde advérsus eos* has no object: *fechai a passagem aos que me perseguem* (the stylist's regency; DRB supplies 'the way', MS1932 'corta a passagem'); *encerrar* is option 3 there.
Ps 34:7 and 34:19 applied (*sem motivo*), 34:7 beside supervácue → *em vão*, as the row foresaw.
Ps 34:7 *supervácue exprobravérunt ánimam meam* → *em vão afrontaram a minha alma* — the blind reader heard 'without success' first, as at 24:4 and 30:7; kept.

Ps 34:4b *cogitántes mihi mala* → *os que pensam em males contra mim*; 34:20 *dolos cogitábant* → *pensavam em enganos* — the stylist wanted a preposition (draft 1 had the bare object) and *tramar*; the row's regency taken, *tramar* option 3 (it explains).
Ps 34:16 *Dissipáti sunt* (people) → *Foram dispersos* — the row's proposal applied.

Ps 34:16 *nec compúncti* → *e não compungidos* (the passive participle, 29:13; the second *foram* dropped with the Latin's ellipsis, after the stylist). The blind reader listed *compungidos* unknown; kept. The stylist's *não sentiram remorso* is option 4.
Ps 34:14 *Quasi próximum* → *como a um próximo*, off the cadence (draft 2 puts the *sic* clause first).
Ps 34:22 *Vidísti, Dómine, ne síleas* → *Vós vistes, Senhor, não fiqueis em silêncio* — applied; the Passiontide responsory; the stylist's best line.
Ps 34:22b *ne discédas a me* → *não vos afasteis de mim* — applied.

Ps 34:28 *tota die laudem tuam* → *o vosso louvor o dia todo* — the object first, so that the Latin's order ('o dia todo o vosso louvor') is not heard as 'all your praise'. The Tuesday Matins versicle (R. *Tota die laudem tuam, Dómine*).
Ps 34:3 *Effúnde frámeam* → *Tirai a espada* (effúndere: MS1932 'Tira da espada'; *Derramai* the calque, *Desembainhai* names a scabbard the Latin lacks).
Ps 34:13b *Humiliábam in jejúnio ánimam meam* → *Humilhava com o jejum a minha alma*; 34:14 *humiliábar* → *eu me humilhava*.
Ps 34:19 *qui adversántur mihi iníque* → *os que injustamente se opõem a mim* (the adverb first, after the stylist; *iniquamente* was unknown to the blind reader).

Ps 34:19 and 34:24 *supergáudeant mihi* → *Não se alegrem à minha custa*. Hostile *super me* elsewhere in Ps 34 (34:16, 34:21, 34:26b) → *contra mim*; the scourges gathered *super me* (34:15) → *sobre mim* (physically upon).

Ps 34:18 *Confitébor tibi in ecclésia magna, * in pópulo gravi laudábo te* → *Eu vos darei graças na grande assembleia, * num povo numeroso vos louvarei* — D5's named verse. gravis → *numeroso* (the Latinist, major on draft 1's *grave*; the blind reader heard 'gravely ill').
Ps 34:18 *in ecclésia magna* → *na grande assembleia* (D34 applied).
Ps 34:7 *intéritum láquei sui* → *a destruição do seu laço* (the Latin's genitive kept; DRB and MS1932 unravel it). Passed the Latinist twice.
Ps 34:7, 34:8 ×2 → *laço*; cáptio beside it → *armadilha* (new row).
Ps 34:26 *Erubéscant et revereántur simul* → *Corem e sejam desonrados juntos* (reveréri, new row).

Ps 34:4 *Confundántur et revereántur* → *Sejam envergonhados e desonrados*; 34:4b *confundántur* → *sejam envergonhados*; 34:26b *confusióne* → *de vergonha*. reveréri beside it needed a third word (new row).
Ps 34:15 *congregáta sunt super me flagélla* → *juntaram-se sobre mim os flagelos*; the blind reader listed *flagelos* unknown again (heard calamities); kept.

terms: | reveréri / reveréntia | ser desonrado / desonra (*Sejam envergonhados e desonrados*; *Vistam-se de vergonha e de desonra*) | open — **for a ruling** | Ps 34:4, 34:26, 34:26b (ἐντρέπεσθαι / ἐντροπή: to be abashed); always beside confúndi or erubéscere, so it needs a third word of shame (confúndi → *ser envergonhado*, D15; erubéscere → *corar*). Draft 1 *vexados / vexame*: unknown to the blind reader twice. *confundidos* (MS1932) is the word D15 took from confúndi. The Latinist, gate (three minors), wanted *envergonhados / confusão* — refused: they swap confúndi's words onto reveréri. Cost: *desonra* is disgrace, where the Latin is abashment. Other places (grep): 39:15 ×2, 69:3 (both near-twins of 34:4), 68:20 *reveréntiam meam*. **Proposal: *desonrar / desonra*; options *vexar*, *confundir*.** |
| coarctáre | apertar (*e que o anjo do Senhor os aperte*) | open | Ps 34:5 only (grep); ἐκθλίβων, press hard. *estreitar* (DRB 'straiten') heard of a thing; *acossar* adds pursuit (34:6 has it). |
| lúbricum (neuter as noun) | lugar escorregadio | open | Ps 34:6 *ténebræ et lúbricum* (ὀλίσθημα); the noun supplied, as 2:1 *coisas vãs*. |
| cáptio | armadilha (*e o apanhe a armadilha que escondeu*) | open | Ps 34:8 (θήρα); DRB and MS1932 *net / rede* — refused, *rede* is rete's (9:16b, 30:5). Beside láqueus → laço in the same verse. |
| sterílitas | esterilidade (*esterilidade para a minha alma*) | open | Ps 34:12 (ἀτεκνία); *ánimæ meæ* taken as dative, with the Greek; *da minha alma* (genitive) the option. |

| molestus (*molésti esse*) | importunar (*quando me importunavam*) | open | Ps 34:13 (παρενοχλεῖν); *molestar* is heard in Brazil as harassment first; *molesto* (MS1932) rare. **54:4 *in ira molésti erant mihi* (the only other place, grep) should follow.** |

| malígnitas | maldade (*da maldade deles*) | open | Ps 34:17 only (grep; κακουργία). *malignidade* heard as medical; *maldade* is nequítia's (7:10) but the two never meet. malígnus → malvado (D24). |

| gratulári | festejar (*os que festejam os meus males*) | open | Ps 34:26 (ἐπιχαίροντες). Draft 1 *se congratulam com* (MS1932): unknown to the blind reader, ceremonial to the stylist; *alegrar-se* (the stylist's) refused, lætári's and supergaudére's in the same psalm. Passed the Latinist. |

| euge | Que bom (*Que bom, que bom, os nossos olhos viram*) | open | Ps 34:21, 34:25 (εὖγε), in the mouths of gloaters. Draft 1 *Bem feito* (said of another's misfortune): the stylist and the blind reader heard 'deserved punishment' at 34:25. 34:25 *ánimæ nostræ* → *para a nossa alma*. **39:16 and 69:4 *qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge* (grep) should copy.** |
| annúere óculis | fazer sinais com os olhos | open | Ps 34:19 (διανεύοντες ὀφθαλμοῖς); *piscar* heard as blinking, *acenar* (MS1932) as waving the hand. |

| retrórsum (*Avertántur / Convertántur retrórsum*) | voltar para trás (*Voltem para trás*) | open | Ps 34:4b (ἀποστραφήτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω); *desviados para trás* is not Portuguese, so neither avértere's *desviar* nor convértere's verb is used alone: the phrase is one Portuguese phrase under either Latin verb (D15's test, one Greek). 39:15, 69:4 (= this colon's start), 128:5 should copy; 9:4, 55:9 *converténtur retrórsum* likely too (grep). |
formulas: | *Confundántur et revereántur, * quæréntes / qui quærunt ánimam meam* (34:4; 69:3; 39:15 with *simul* and *ut áuferant eam*) | *Sejam envergonhados e desonrados, * os que buscam a minha alma* | working (Ps 34) |
| *Avertántur retrórsum, et confundántur / erubéscant* (34:4b; 69:4) | *Voltem para trás, e sejam envergonhados / e corem* | working (Ps 34) |
